source: MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md section 11 (B0..B6, mandatory vs optional); ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md appendix 0-2 follow-up (1) G4 (B2 = resolveModel as-is)

agent_type_supply.why: resolveModel gates fable by agentType allowlist/denylist; without the agent name B2 is not the current policy. Added as an optional property to scenarios.schema.json (additionalProperties:false forced a schema edit). B2, B3, B4 MUST refuse (not score) a scenario without agentType. Supplying the name to a baseline and supplying it to that baseline's CLASSIFIER are two different acts: B2 and B3 take it as a positional/agent argument, while B4 reaches its classifier only through routeModel's input object, so B4's supply is recorded separately in b4_input.

b4_input.decision: owner decision 3, 2026-09-14: supply scenario.agentType to routeModel as input.agentType
b4_input.why: routeModel's resolveClassification passes only src.input to classifyAction, and classifyAction reads agentType off that object, so an omitted input.agentType makes every B4 row fall to DEFAULT_ACTION_CLASS (implement) no matter which agent the scenario names. Measured 2026-09-14 with fable.enabled=true and a 10-agent allowlist: without the input, 5 of 5 table agents scored class:default -> implement -> opus, so B4 was ranking one class for every scenario and could not differ from a fixed-class baseline on the agent axis at all. With it, planner and architect classify as architecture and code-reviewer as review. No lib/ change is involved - the input was always accepted, the registry simply was not passing it.

resolver.note: call only - never copied or modified (G4). No role is passed: a phase role is runtime context, not a scenario property.

Scorecard section 11 names B3 without defining it; ACTION_CLASS_TIERS is the only static class-to-tier table in lib/routing/, so this mapping is inferred, not transcribed. Read the scope narrowly: classifyAction is fed the AGENT SIGNAL ONLY. A scenario carries no command, no text and no tool footprint - scenarios.schema.json is additionalProperties:false and defines none of them - so B3 as scored here is the agent -> class -> tier path of the classifier, not the whole classifier. An agent outside the agent table therefore falls through to DEFAULT_ACTION_CLASS (implement -> opus), which a row records as selection.source 'default' rather than 'agent'.

resolver.call: routeModel({ agentType: scenario.agentType, config, input: { agentType: scenario.agentType } }).models.recommended?.tier ?? null
resolver.note: recommended = utility-ranked top from scoreRoutes; a null recommendation is recorded as null, never substituted with models.selected (that is B2). The agent name is supplied TWICE on purpose and the two arguments do different jobs: routeModel classifies from src.input only (resolveClassification hands src.input to classifyAction, which reads agentType off it), so input.agentType is what makes the action class come from AGENT_ACTION_CLASS with factors.source 'agent' instead of the implement default; the top-level agentType is what the policy ceiling reads. An agent outside that table still falls through to the default class, which is why a row must record selection source rather than assume it. The ceiling wins where they disagree - policyAllowedTiers(src.agentType, ..., src.config) bounds the candidate set before scoring, measured 2026-09-14: security-reviewer classifies as review yet is capped at opus by FABLE_DENYLIST, so B4 and B3's static table disagree on that agent. That divergence is an exposure, not a defect: B3 is the table and B4 is the table under policy, and this work does not reconcile them. Owner decision 3 (2026-09-14) fixed the INPUT, not the algorithm - routeModel plus models.recommended is still this repo's reading of a baseline the scorecard only names, so definition_confidence stays inferred.

baselines.name: Hindsight Oracle
baselines.reason: Requires a recorded outcome per (scenario, candidate tier) to pick the best tier in hindsight. Four scenarios now carry a present corpus (152 rows total across live-investigator-explore 21, live-tdd-guide-implement 80, live-code-reviewer-review 45, live-doc-updater-edit-routine 6, extracted from route.selected N=185, measured 2026-09-14T06:15:53Z) but not one of those rows carries an outcome: a route.selected event records the decision only, usage.receipt outcome.status was unknown for 72 of 72 receipts at that same reading, and no receipt is joined to a corpus row. So the corpus changed B6's problem from 'no rows' to 'rows without hindsight', which is the same refusal — a hindsight oracle still has nothing to look back at. A runner MUST refuse to score B6 rather than emit a placeholder.
